messages:
omar: Hey folks, Omar here (first week). I followed the k8s onboarding but `kubectl get pods -n batch-jobs` returns `Error from server (Forbidden)`.
Does onboarding grant access to the batch-jobs namespace by default or do I need to request it? Also my kubeconfig shows two redwood contexts (redwood-staging, redwood-dev) so not sure which to use.

celia (infra): welcome @omar! :wave: We don't auto-grant every new hire access to team namespaces. For batch-jobs you need to be in the `batch-engineers` SSO group or get a temporary RoleBinding. What's your SSO email?

omar: omar.ali@redwood.ai

jen (devex): fyi onboarding doc has a checklist but it assumes you join team groups. Quick step: run `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts` then switch to the environment your team uses. Mara from ML owns batch-jobs so i'm cc'ing her.

mara (ml): hey @omar, hi @celia. batch-jobs is ML infra for nightly runs, we keep it view-only for most new folks. If you need to inspect logs or check job status we can give `view`. Who on your team needs edit/port-forward later?

omar: for now just view and logs. might ask for port-forward next week when pairing on a debug.

celia (infra): got it. i'll open a short-lived RoleBinding (48h) for view in `batch-jobs` for your SSO account and start the group invite to `batch-engineers` which gives permanent access. Applying this now — YAML preview:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-view-omar-ali
  namespace: batch-jobs
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: "omar.ali@redwood.ai"
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
``` 

ops-bot: INFRA-1337 created by celia (infra): "temp view binding for omar.ali in batch-jobs". ETA: 5m.

celia (infra): small troubleshooting note: if your kubeconfig has merged files and points to `redwood-staging` instead of `redwood-dev`, you might hit the wrong cluster. Commands to check:

`kubectl config current-context`
`kubectl config get-contexts | grep redwood`
`echo $KUBECONFIG`

Switch with `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev` (or redwood-staging depending on which environment your team uses). If you see TLS or token expiry errors re-run the SSO script in the onboarding doc.

omar: current-context was `redwood-staging`, switched to `redwood-dev` and re-run. Still got Forbidden, but `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n batch-jobs --as omar.ali@redwood.ai` returned `no` before the ticket.

ops-bot: INFRA-1337 status: applied.

celia (infra): binding applied. test with `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n batch-jobs --as omar.ali@redwood.ai` and then `kubectl get pods -n batch-jobs`.

omar: `can-i` now returns yes and `kubectl get pods -n batch-jobs` lists pods. nice! thanks so much :tada:

mara (ml): i'll add you to the `batch-engineers` group tomorrow so you don't need temp bindings. @leo (eng) — tagging you in case you want to show Omar the job naming conventions.

leo (eng): happy to give a 10-min orientation. ping me and i'll share a short doc with common kubectl incantations we use for batch jobs (how to tail logs, find recent jobs, etc).

jen (devex): noted — adding a step to the onboarding checklist to explicitly check the current-context and echo $KUBECONFIG. linking the internal doc here: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/k8s-handoff (has screenshots and SSO tips).

omar: everything works now. Appreciate the fast help everyone — excited to be here!
